thread:
maya: Heads-up — BigCommerce pilot asked for 2x burst for marketing spikes but only for 48h windows. They want guarantees in the contract. Need product + eng decision by EOD Friday.
liam: Do we know expected qps spike shape? 2x peak or steady for 48h?
maya: @liam they said 'sustained 2x' for roughly 36-48h during promos. Customer willing to pay for reserved buffer but wants clear failover rules.
arjun: Two quick levers: (1) short-term burst credits on top of reserved pools, or (2) temporary capacity bump (pre-provision) with rollback. Tradeoffs: credits = simpler infra, bump = predictable latency.
sasha: For contract wording we need clear SLA changes if we accept burst guarantees. Also need billing model: prepaid credits vs overage at premium rate.
emily: From infra POV, temporary bumps require capacity planning lead time. If they book 48h ahead it's doable via scheduling. On-demand 2x without booking risks other customers.
paul: Can we do a hybrid? Allow up to X% of reserved pool as "soft burst" with priority rules, plus guaranteed reserved instances when customer prepays for a "hard burst" slot.
carol: Need to align with Dedicated product roadmap. We have autoscale work in Q3 — this feature could be a small scoped extension if we pin launch criteria.
maya: Proposal: ship a beta "burst-reserve" feature: customer can (A) book a time window up to 72h with 48h lead, or (B) buy burst credits that consume under contention. Beta launch criteria: docs, billing flow, canary rollback, and a guardrail that we never exceed reserved region capacity.
liam: Engineering constraints: implement policy layer + scheduler + billing hook. Rough estimate: 3 sw sprints + 1 for SRE runbook. Need a simpler default policy for beta:

```
policy:
  mode: "booked" # booked | credit
  lead_time_hours: 48
  max_multiplier: 2.0
  preemptible: true
  fallback: route-to-hosted
```

That gets us basic behavior without deep autoscale changes.
arjun: Fallback route-to-hosted is fine but we must define cost and latency SLO downgrade policy in contract language.
sasha: Contract clause draft (short): "During booked burst windows Redwood will attempt to honor up to N x baseline capacity. In cases where physical capacity constraints occur, Redwood will route excess traffic to the hosted tier and apply pre-agreed premium credits/backfill or offer refund credits."
paul: Ops concern: monitoring and runbooks. ops-bot should send alert if booked utilization > 85% for more than 15m.
ops-bot: :robot_face: Alert rule suggestion: "booked_burst_utilization >= 0.85 for 15m" -> Pager to oncall.
emily: Also add a cooldown policy after a booked window to avoid thrash: 6h cooldown where we deprioritize non-booked bursts.
carol: Roadmap callout: mark as "beta: contractual pilots only" and target 6-week delivery if we prioritize next sprint. Otherwise Q3 larger autoscale plan.
maya: Customer asks: they want commitment in contract now. Options: (1) promise subject to region capacity — faster, (2) promise with prepaid capacity — slower but firmer. Which do we recommend?
liam: Recommend (2) prepaid capacity for production SLAs. (1) ok for pilot with explicit fallback.
arjun: Agree. For kickoff, offer pilot under (1) with clear fallback + quick upgrade path to (2).
sasha: I'll draft contract language for pilot vs production commitments and circulate.
maya: Action items: @sasha draft contract, @liam + @emily scope infra work and sprint estimate, @paul write monitoring/runbook, @carol slot roadmap and decide prioritization by Wed, @maya prep customer communication. We'll reconvene Thu AM.
paul: I'll add the runbook stub to ops-playbooks and link it in this thread when done.
liam: Will do a short RFC for the policy layer, post by EOD Tue.
maya: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
